title: An analysis of daylighting performance for office buildings in Hong Kong

findings.antecedent: floor and internal room surface areas
findings.mechanism: larger surface areas dilute the incoming light flux
findings.quote: The bigger the floor and internal room surface areas, the smaller will be the average DF.

findings.antecedent: vertical outdoor illuminances
findings.mechanism: direct relationship between external vertical light and internal light penetration
findings.quote: More vertical outdoor illuminances contribute to higher amount of indoor daylight levels.

findings.antecedent: room depth too long compared to room width and height
findings.consequent: rear half of room looks shadowy and requires supplementary electric lighting
findings.mechanism: insufficient light penetration into deep plan areas
findings.quote: If the depth of the room from window to back wall is too long comparing with the room width and height, then rear half of the room tends to look shadowy compared to the brightly-lit front half and supplement electric lighting will be required for most of daytime.

findings.antecedent: higher window heads and wider spaces
findings.mechanism: larger window openings allow light to penetrate further into a room
findings.quote: Higher window heads and wider spaces allow deeper plan room designs.

findings.antecedent: light transmittance of glazing
findings.mechanism: direct proportionality in daylight calculation
findings.quote: In daylight calculation, light transmittance is directly proportion to the daylight factor.

findings.antecedent: clear glass glazing
findings.consequent: daylight transmission (visible transmittance of 0.88) AND solar heat gain (high shading coefficient)
findings.mechanism: material properties of clear glass allow high visible light and solar radiation to pass through
findings.quote: Clear glass provides a high transmission of daylight with typical visible transmittance (VT) of 0.88 but it also allows a large amount of solar heat (high shading coefficient) to pass through into a building.

findings.antecedent: tinted glass glazing
findings.consequent: visible light transmission (VT ranges from 0.23 to 0.51)
findings.mechanism: tinting absorbs visible light
findings.quote: Tinted glass absorbs a considerable amount of infrared with some reduction of visible light. The VT ranges from 0.23 to 0.51.

findings.antecedent: reflective glass glazing
findings.consequent: visible light transmission (VT of 0.12), daylight factor, and visual comfort
findings.mechanism: reflective coating reduces visible light transmission, leading to gloomy interiors and discomfort
findings.quote: The VT can be of 0.12 and the rooms may look gloomy with low DF under overcast skies. This may cause visual discomfort to occupants.

findings.antecedent: reflective glass glazing
findings.mechanism: reflective coating absorbs more heat than tinted glass
findings.quote: Reflective glass absorbs more heat than tinted glass and offers good reflecting characteristic in the infrared region with a certain reduction of VT.

findings.antecedent: low-e glass glazing
findings.mechanism: metal oxide coating cuts down heat gain
findings.quote: Low-e glass contains a thin coating of metal oxide substantially cutting down heat gain without proportionally reducing daylight transmittance.

findings.antecedent: low-e glass glazing
findings.consequent: daylight transmittance reduction (relative to heat gain reduction)
findings.mechanism: metal oxide coating reduces heat gain without proportionally reducing daylight transmittance
findings.quote: Low-e glass contains a thin coating of metal oxide substantially cutting down heat gain without proportionally reducing daylight transmittance.

findings.antecedent: exterior shading devices (overhangs and side-fins) compared to interior shading devices (venetian blinds and curtain blinds)
findings.consequent: effectiveness in blocking direct sunlight and solar heat
findings.mechanism: exterior devices intercept solar radiation before it enters the building envelope
findings.quote: Exterior shading devices frequently found in Hong Kong for office buildings include overhangs and side-fins which are more effective to block the direct sunlight and solar heat than interior shading devices such as venetian blinds and curtain blinds.

findings.antecedent: buildings located close to each other, particularly for lower floors
findings.mechanism: physical obstruction of the sky view by adjacent buildings
findings.quote: When buildings are located close to each other, blockage of natural daylight can be severe, particularly for the lower floors.

findings.antecedent: surrounding buildings with light colour surface finish
findings.consequent: externally reflected component (ERC) and internally reflected component (IRC) values
findings.mechanism: light-colored surfaces reflect more light into the building interior
findings.quote: Surrounding buildings with light colour surface finish tend to give large ERC and IRC values.

findings.antecedent: high reflectance from nearby obstructions
findings.mechanism: excessive luminance contrast from reflected light sources
findings.quote: However, high reflectance from nearby obstructions may cause glare problems.

findings.antecedent: top floors of Building 30 with no large external obstructions
findings.mechanism: unobstructed sky view allows maximum daylight penetration
findings.quote: The simulated DFs are in the range of 8.4-8.8% at the point of 0.5m away from the windows for various orientations.

findings.antecedent: lower floors (1/F) of Building 30 in the southwest zone with obstructing buildings
findings.mechanism: obstruction blocks sky view, reducing incident daylight
findings.quote: DF decreases from 8.7% at 33/F to 5.3% at 1/F for the southwest zone.

findings.antecedent: northeast zone of Building 30 with an obstruction angle of 22°
findings.consequent: daylight factor (DF) at different floor levels
findings.mechanism: low obstruction angle has minimal impact on DF across floors
findings.quote: With 0=22°, there is almost no change in DF at different floor levels for northeast zone.

findings.antecedent: room depth of 7m (half room depth) away from window facades in Building 30
findings.mechanism: light levels diminish rapidly with distance from the window
findings.quote: At room depth of 7 m (half room depth), the DFs reduce to less than 0.7% for all floors and zones.

findings.antecedent: top and middle floors of Building 20 in south and west zones at 0.5m from windows
findings.mechanism: proximity to window and favorable orientation allows good daylight penetration
findings.quote: The DF is around 5.5%, 0.5 m away from the windows on the top and middle floors for the south and west zones.

findings.antecedent: lower floor (5/F) of Building 20 in south and west zones with non-severe shading
findings.mechanism: even non-severe shading can slightly reduce daylight levels at lower floors
findings.quote: As the shading effect is not severe, the DFs at 5/F for these two zones slightly reduce to 5%.

findings.antecedent: increased distance from window (near internal core) in Building 20
findings.mechanism: light levels diminish rapidly with distance from the window, especially in deep plans
findings.quote: As the points are far away from the apertures, the simulated DFs drop rapidly. The DF can be less than 0.2% near the internal core.

findings.antecedent: north zone of Building 20 with a large obstruction angle of 64°
findings.mechanism: significant obstruction blocks a large portion of the sky, reducing incident daylight
findings.quote: Similar characteristics can be found for the north zone but with lower DF levels due to the large 0 of 64° appearing at the north orientation.

findings.antecedent: average daylight factor (DF) of 5% or more
findings.consequent: interior looks substantially daylight AND electric lighting not normally used during daytime
findings.mechanism: sufficient natural light provides visual comfort and reduces reliance on artificial lighting
findings.quote: An average DF of 5% or more will ensure that an interior looks substantially daylight and electric lighting is not normally to be used during daytime (i.e. office hours).

findings.antecedent: average daylight factor (DF) below 2%
findings.consequent: room looks dull AND artificial lighting likely in frequent use
findings.mechanism: insufficient natural light leads to poor visual quality and increased need for artificial lighting
findings.quote: An average DF below 2% generally makes a room look dull and artificial lighting is likely to be in frequent use.

findings.antecedent: proper daylighting (perimeter zone fully lit, intermediate zone 50% lit by daylight) in Building 30
findings.mechanism: reduced reliance on artificial lighting due to natural light availability
findings.quote: Accordingly, it was deduced that the building lighting energy could be significantly decreased by around 25% and 20% for Buildings 30 and 20, respectively.

findings.antecedent: proper daylighting (perimeter zone fully lit, intermediate zone 50% lit by daylight) in Building 20
findings.mechanism: reduced reliance on artificial lighting due to natural light availability
findings.quote: Accordingly, it was deduced that the building lighting energy could be significantly decreased by around 25% and 20% for Buildings 30 and 20, respectively.

findings.antecedent: less electric light fittings used (due to daylighting)
findings.mechanism: artificial lighting generates sensible heat gains, so reducing its use reduces cooling load
findings.quote: Further savings in cooling energy and heat rejection could be obtained due to less sensible heat gains generated by artificial lighting fittings.

findings.antecedent: less electric light fittings used (due to daylighting) during cold winter days
findings.mechanism: artificial lighting contributes to internal heat gain, so reducing its use increases heating demand in cold conditions
findings.quote: During cold winter days, heating energy if required, may be increased when less electric light fittings are used.

findings.antecedent: Building 30
findings.mechanism: descriptive range of simulated glare
findings.quote: It can be seen that the DGI for Building 30 is of a smaller variation, ranging between 15.9 and 19.6.

findings.antecedent: northwest and northeast zones of Building 30
findings.mechanism: orientation relative to sun path and external obstructions can influence glare
findings.quote: the DGI for the northwest and northeast zones are higher than those for the southeast and southwest zones.

findings.antecedent: Building 20
findings.mechanism: descriptive range of simulated glare
findings.quote: The DGI varies in a great deal, ranging from 10.9 to just over 19.

findings.antecedent: high floor levels (Buildings 20 and 30)
findings.mechanism: higher floors have less external obstruction, leading to greater sky luminance and potential for glare
findings.quote: Generally, large DGIs appear in high floor levels.

findings.antecedent: DGI less than 22 (for Buildings 20 and 30 under overcast skies)
findings.mechanism: DGI below the threshold indicates acceptable visual comfort
findings.quote: With the threshold DGI of 22 [28], there will be no discomfort glare for the two buildings under overcast skies.

stimuli.description: 3D computer models of two office buildings (Building 20 and 30) including exterior obstructions and sky conditions for simulation.

tables.description: Summary of daylight parameter for 35 surveyed buildings, including building and site conditions and glazing information.
Ambient parameters setting for RADIANCE simulation for Building 20 and Building 30.
Calculated areas for different daylight zones (perimeter, intermediate, inner) for high, middle, and low floors of Buildings 20 and 30.
Calculated limiting room depths at different orientations for Buildings 20 and 30.
Daylight glare index (DGI) values for different directions and floor levels for Buildings 20 and 30.

limitations: Energy savings are deduced and estimated based on assumptions from simulation, not direct field measurements.
Simulation uses CIE overcast sky conditions, which may not represent all real-world sky conditions (e.g., clear skies).
The study acknowledges that average Daylight Factor (DF) alone does not provide information on the diversity of illuminance within the space.
